title: Germany – Architectural and related services – Erweiterung Schulcampus Preysingstraße mit Offener Ganztagsschule (OGTS) und Hort
description: Es wird ein nichtoffener Realisierungswettbewerb mit anschließendem Verhandlungsverfahren durchgeführt. Anhand der Auswahlkriterien werden 15 Teilnehmer für die Teilnahme am Wettbewerb ermittelt. Bei gleichwertigen Anträgen bleibt vorbehalten, das Los entscheiden zu lassen. Die Teilnahme am Planungswettbewerb ist Architekten in verpflichtender Zusammenarbeit mit Landschaftsarchitekten vorbehalten. Der Wettbewerb ist mit der Bayerischen Architektenkammer abgestimmt. Das Verfahren ist anonym. Die Namen der Teilnehmenden werden den Mitgliedern des Preisgerichts erst nach Abschluss der Entscheidung des Preisgerichts bekannt gemacht. Die Wettbewerbssprache ist Deutsch. Die Stadt Plattling plant nördlich der Grundschule Plattling einen Neubau für die offene Ganztagsschule und den Hort. Im Zuge des Neubaus soll auch die Preysingstraße im Bereich zwischen Bestand und Neubau im Sinne eines verkehrsberuhigten Campus für mehr Sicherheit für die Schüler*innen umgestaltet werden. Ziel des Wettbewerbs ist es, einen zusammenhängenden Schulcampus zu schaffen, der die bestehende Grundschule um einen Neubau mit Räumlichkeiten für die Offene Ganztagsschule (OGTS) und den Hort ergänzt und sinnvoll miteinander vernetzt, qualitative Freiräume mit Aufenthaltsqualität schafft und die Verkehrssicherheit für die Schüler*innen erhöht. Das Wettbewerbsgebiet ist 12.039 m² groß. Der Auftraggeber wird, wenn das Projekt realisiert wird, unter Würdigung der Empfehlungen des Preisgerichts einen der Preisträger mit den weiteren Planungsleistungen beauftragen. Es wird hierzu ein Verhandlungsverfahren nach § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 VgV durchgeführt. Der Auftraggeber behält sich vor, zunächst nur mit dem Gewinner und im Falle des Scheiterns dieser Verhandlungen mit allen Preisträgern oder gleich mit allen Preisträgern zu verhandeln. Bei Verhandlungen mit allen Preisträgern wird das Ergebnis des Wettbewerbs mit mindestens 40 % gewichtet. Die weiteren Zuschlagskriterien und deren Gewichtung werden mit der Aufforderung zur Teilnahme an der Verhandlung bekannt geben. Der Bauherr schließt mit dem Sieger des Verhandlungsverfahrens Verträge über die weiteren Planungsleistungen zur Umsetzung des Wettbewerbsentwurfs und der Erweiterung der bestehenden Mensa in der Bestandsgrundschule ab. Beschreibung Auftragsversprechen Mensaerweiterung: Aufgrund der wachsenden Anzahl an Schüler*innen und dem bundesweiten Ganztagsanspruchs ab dem Schuljahr 2026/27 erfüllt die bestehende Mensa der Grundschule Plattling nicht mehr den benötigten Sitzplatzbedarf. Um den wachsenden Anforderungen gerecht zu werden, muss die bestehende Mensa um mindestens 105 m² erweitert werden. Die Erweiterung der Bestandsmensa ist Teil des Auftragsversprechens, jedoch nicht Teil der Entwurfsaufgabe des Realisierungswettbewerbs. Es wird eine stufenweise Beauftragung folgender Leistungsphasen vorgesehen: • § 34 HOAI 2021 „Gebäude und Innenräume“ mit den Leistungsphasen 1-9 • § 39 HOAI 2021 „Freianlagen“ mit den Leistungsphasen 1-9 Im Falle einer Realisierung werden, zur Sicherstellung der Qualität bei der Umsetzung des Wettbewerbsentwurfs, mindestens die Leistungsphasen 1 bis einschließlich 5 der Leistungsbilder „Gebäude und Innenräume“ und „Freianlagen“ beauftragt, außer es stehen dem wichtige Gründe entgegen. Es werden zunächst die Leistungsphasen 1 bis 2 in beiden Leistungsbildern beauftragt. Im Weiteren werden voraussichtlich weitere Leistungsphasen stufenweise beauftragt. Ein Anspruch auf Beauftragung aller Leistungsphasen besteht nicht. Die Beauftragung der Leistungsstufe 1 soll in der zweiten Jahreshälfte 2027 erfolgen. Der Baubeginn soll 2028, der Abschluss der Maßnahme Ende 2029 erfolgen. Soweit nicht etwas anderes bestimmt ist, wird der Wettbewerb nach den Regeln der RPW 2013 durchgeführt. Die Bruttogeschossfläche des Neubaus der OGTS und Hort liegt bei ca. 1.500 m²

title: Ireland – Construction work – Multi-Party Framework Agreement for Civil Engineering Works at Dublin Port
description: DPC proposes to engage in a competitive process for the establishment of a Multi-Party Framework Agreement for the provision of Civil Engineering Works at Dublin Port and other lands under DPC’s control. The Framework will be concluded under the EU Utilities Directive 2014/25/EU and the associated Irish Statutory Instrument, S.I. No. 286 of 2016, implementing that Directive with binding force, specificity, precision and clarity, under Ireland’s obligations under the EU Treaty. It is acknowledged that the full scope of services cannot be defined, as it will be influenced by the conditions of regulatory consents/licences yet to be issued. As and when required, DPC will procure these works under the Framework. The successful Framework Members will be required to carry out civil engineering works in connection with DPC’s Masterplan projects and associated capital works projects at Dublin Port. The works listed below, although non-exhaustive, may be required under the Framework and delivered to the satisfaction of DPC, as included in the Masterplan Projects, including Alexandra Basin Redevelopment / MP2 / 3FM, which include the following: • Dismantling of infrastructure and removal of infill material • Quay wall refurbishment/construction (designed to accommodate future dredging to a level of -15.0m CD) • Installation of Ro-Ro ramps. • Ro-Ro jetty works. • Dredging of basin and berths. • Treatment of contaminated dredged material and re-use as infill on site. • Development of cultural heritage interpretative space. • Infilling of existing Berths (including where appropriate with treated dredged material). • Raising of existing surface levels. • Mooring jetty construction. • Construction of surge protection/retaining wall. • Surfacing of areas behind key walls using a combination of concrete slabs and bituminous surfacing or block paving for terminal yards/roads. • Wall Protection Works, including concrete Mattresses being lifted into position. • Port equipment, including relocation and refurbishment of existing ramps. • The relocation of loading operations to a new quay across the Port. • Internal road and bridge construction works throughout the Port. • Port-related buildings. • Specialist equipment supply (e.g. Loading Arms, Conveyor Systems, Fixed/Mobile Cranes, STS, specialist pipeline (e.g. Oil, Gas and the like). • Port Electrification upgrade infrastructure works. • Core civil engineering works including roads, pavements and hardstanding; drainage and utilities infrastructure; earthworks and ground remediation; civil structures (retaining walls, culverts, bridges); marine and quay-adjacent civil works; • DPC reserves the right to include additional ancillary works or enabling works as required to deliver the masterplan projects, including but not limited to, Additional/related services: site enabling works, temporary works design, traffic management during construction to facilitate the civil engineering works. DPC is seeking only candidates capable of delivering the full range of works listed above, whether in-house or as a grouping/consortium. Applications relating to only one or several of these disciplines will be rejected.

title: Norway – Systems and technical consultancy services – Procurement of consultancy services for nuclear security, including handling used fuel, radiation protection and risk assessment.
description: The consultant agreement shall cover the provision of technical services in support of DSA ́s core functions within regulatory work. The work shall include reviewing and assessing technical documentation and support for DSA in connection with inspections. There are three nuclear plants in Norway: the research reactor facilities in Kjeller and Halden, and the combined landfill and storage facility for low and medium radioactive waste in Himdalen. In 2018 the Norwegian government established a new government organisation, Norsk Nukleærdekommisjonering (NND), which will take over all Norwegian nuclear power plants in Kjeller, Halden and Himdalen from the original operator, Institute for Energy Engineering (IFE). NND will be responsible for the operation of the nuclear installations, the production of them and the handling of radioactive waste and used core fuel. So far the nuclear power plant in Halden has been transferred from IFE to NND, and the other two installations are close to being transferred. Before the shutdown can start, there are a number of processes that must be completed so that the operator(s) shall be able to make changes in the installations in a safe and responsible manner, and for the regulation authority (DSA) to be able to approve changes in accordance with regulations and international standards. In preparation for the liquidation and during the shutdown, there will be a need to establish a new waste handling facility, including plans for a US-developed mobile melt consolidation facility (MMC). The procurement is covered by the Security Act and reflected in the contracting authority ́s requirement specifications and security requirements. Tenderers who would like to offer in this procurement are asked separately to familiarise themselves with the stated guidelines, prerequisites and requirements.

title: Maahuolintapalvelut

Hankinnan kohteena on ensisijaisesti ulkomailla tapahtuviin kriisinhallintatehtäviin lähetettävien tai sieltä saapuvien materiaalien sekä henkilöstön maahuolinta. Lisäksi hankinnan kohteena on Suomeen saapuvan ja lähtevän puolustusmateriaalin ja henkilöstön maahuolintaa millä tahansa hankinnan osa-alueen lentokentällä. Maahuolintapalveluilla tarkoitetaan lentokoneen laskeutumisen ja nousun välisenä aikana tehtäviä palveluita. Saapuvat tai lähetevät lentokoneet voivat olla matkustaja-, rahti- tai sotilaskoneita, joiden maahuolinnalle tulee antaa konetyyppikohtainen hinta (ks. liite 2). Lisäksi on erillishinnoiteltavia palveluita kuten esim. de-icing, toilet- ja vesipalvelu, jotka tulee pystyä tuottamaan tarvittaessa. Ilmarahti ja matkatavarat tulee purkaa tai lastata kyytiin ja matkustajille tulee pystyä tarjomaan palveluita. Tarvittavien palveluiden tarve ja volyymi vaihtelee kenttäkohtaisesti. Kunnossapidon sisältö, valmistelutyöt, laatuvaatimukset, kunnossapitoluokat ja toimenpideajat ilmenevät urakkaohjelmasta ja tehtäväkorteista. Osa-alueet 2 ja 3 ovat erikseen hinnoiteltavia kohdeoptioita; niiden käyttöönotosta päätetään tarjousasiakirjoissa ilmoitetun menettelyn mukaisesti. Kohdeoption tarjoaminen tai tarjouksen hyväksyminen ei yksin velvoita tilaajaa tilaamaan kohdetta. Sopimuskausi on 1.12.2026–15.6.2028. Hankintaan sisältyy mahdollisuus kahteen erilliseen yhden vuoden optiokauteen (1+1), jotka kattavat talvikaudet 2028–2029 ja 2029–2030. Optiokausien käyttöönotosta päättää tilaaja erikseen urakkasopimuksessa määritellyin ehdoin. Tilaajalla ei ole velvollisuutta käyttää optioita. description: LVNL wenst één geschikte dienstverlener te selecteren die LVNL zelfstandig en langdurig kan ondersteunen bij het beheer, onderhoud en de doorontwikkeling van het ServiceNow-platform, inclusief de daarop gebaseerde modules, scoped applicaties en integraties. De nadruk ligt op het waarborgen van continuïteit, beschikbaarheid, kwaliteit, veiligheid en toekomstbestendigheid van het platform. De dienstverlener levert hiervoor specialistische ondersteuningsdiensten in de vorm van Managed Services voor beheer en Consultancy voor doorontwikkeling. Van de leverancier wordt verwacht dat deze optreedt als strategische en uitvoerende ServiceNow-partner voor LVNL. De leverancier levert technisch applicatiebeheer, ondersteunt bij lifecycle management en upgrades, voert configuratiewijzigingen uit, adviseert over platformontwikkeling en licentiegebruik en ondersteunt LVNL bij wijzigingen, uitbreidingen en implementatie van nieuwe functionaliteit. Zie de Offerteleidraad voor de volledige omschrijving. Binnen LVNL wordt ServiceNow gebruikt als strategisch platform voor IT Service Management (ITSM) en de ondersteuning van diverse bedrijfsprocessen. Naast de standaard ServiceNow-functionaliteit zijn op het platform aanvullende applicaties ontwikkeld, waaronder EWR. Het platform wordt beheerd door LVNL, ondersteund door een externe specialistische ServiceNow-partner. LVNL wenst een duurzame samenwerking aan te gaan met één leverancier die het beheer, de ondersteuning en de doorontwikkeling van het platform kan verzorgen. title: COOP Wharf Elevation Works at L'Étang-du-Nord Fishing Harbour, Magdalen Islands, Quebec
description: The elevation works for the COOP Wharf at L’Étang-du-Nord Fishing Harbour in the Magdalen Islands include, but are not limited to, the following work: • Partial demolition of existing wharves and reuse of recovered stone. • Installation of a containment curtain and a floating boom to retain driftwood and suspended particles during wharf demolition or dredging activities required for preparation of the granular foundation. • Excavation of the seabed (contaminated sediments) to allow for the installation of the granular foundation for the new crib structures. • Work required for the installation of the granular foundation of the new timber crib wharves. • Supply of all materials required for the construction of ACC-treated timber crib wharves. • Demolition of the riprap protection on one side of the wharf approach. • Placement of pit run and granular materials for the widening of the wharf approach. • Stockpiling (according to potential contamination) and characterization of dredged materials to construct the granular base for the new crib structures. • Disposal and/or beneficial use of dredged sediments at authorized sites. • Civil works for the installation of electrical and potable water services to the new wharf. • Paving works for the wharf approach. • Supply and installation of electrical distribution, lighting and water system components.

title: Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade
description: DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – Project No. HQ04022_88127 – Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade, Gagetown, NB DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – Project No. HQ04022_88127 – Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade, Gagetown, NB Defence Construction Canada (DCC) invites general contractors to express their interest in providing all labour, materials, and equipment necessary for the Enniskillen Road Upgrade at Gagetown, NB This Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) is the first step of a two-step solicitation process, the second step being the Tender Phase.  Only general contractors that have expressed their interest through the Electronic Bidding System prior to the closing date and time of this RFEOI will be invited to submit a proposal at the second stage. Only submissions received in accordance with the requirements of the Electronic Bidding System will be considered. Only the general contractors who will have responded to this RFEOI will be invited to submit a bid during the Tender Phase. DCC reserves the right to terminate this solicitation at the end of the RFEOI. As part of Canada’s commitment to maximize the participation of Indigenous Businesses, bidders are advised that this solicitation includes an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP). The Contractor will have to include Indigenous businesses (or eligible joint ventures) as subcontractors or suppliers to this project. Further details will be provided in the Tender phase. This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA). Project background A detailed project background can be reviewed in the Building Summary Documents Technical plans and specifications are not available during this RFEOI and will be provided during the Tender Phase; however, the Standard Construction Contract Documents for Electronic Bidding, DCL 250E, are available on DCC's website: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. Tenderers are advised that this contract is subject to DCC's Procurement Code of Conduct, which can be downloaded at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or supplier who has been declared ineligible or suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and whose period of ineligibility or suspension may not have expired will not be able to proceed to the second stage. Bid security will be required during the Tender Phase in accordance with DCL193E- Instructions for Bidders for Electronic Bidding item 5. Estimate The Rough Order Magnitude estimate / Construction Cost Limit for this Contract is $ 25,642,471.00. This amount includes all construction costs, on-site work (including all required services, parking, and landscaping), site utilities, necessary redundant mechanical systems, communication conduits and wiring, backup power equipment, built-in equipment, built-in furniture, and inflation to achieve substantial completion. This amount excludes HST, design costs, travel and disbursements, consultant fees and expenses, movable equipment and furniture, IT equipment and contingencies. Schedule DCC will proceed with the Tender Phase around November - December 2026. The works shall reach substantial completion no later than October 15, 2027 and shall be completed no later than November 15, 2027.\ Site visit No site visits will be offered during the RFEOI however, during the Tender Phase, bidders will be invited to a site visit. Access to information Act Tenderers are advised that DCC is subject to the provisions of the Access to Information Act (Canada). Information submitted may be eligible for disclosure in accordance with the requirements of the Act. Questions and clarifications Any questions or requests for clarification must be submitted in writing to DCC's Coordinator, Contract Services whose contact information can be found in the Electronic Bid System. DCC reserves the right to request clarification and/or confirmation regarding any aspect of this RFEOI to the Tenderer. In such a case, the Coordinator, Contract Services will be responsible for making the request. The request for clarification and/or confirmation will be sent to the contact person identified on the Electronic Submission System. Language of the Tender and the contract By submitting a response to this RFEOI, Tenderers will be invited to choose the desired official language for the tender documents and any resulting contract. In the Tender Phase, tender documents will be published in the language chosen by the Tenderer in the Electronic Bid System. title: Inspect and Repair of 13.2KV Main Switchgear
description: The U.S. Coast Guard Academy requires a qualified, licensed electrical contractor to inspect, repair as necessary, test, and restore Eaton/Cutler-Hammer MVS2 13.2 kV medium-voltage load interrupter switchgear, with primary work focused on Cabinet 5 and the associated 15 kV feeder cable serving Smith Hall. title: LETTER OF INTEREST (LOI) – DETERMINATION OF V50 VELOCITIES FOR SELECTED PROJECTILES
description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) Specialized Firearms Support Services (SFSS) supports firearms classification activities, including determining whether certain devices meet the definition of a firearm under section 2 of the Criminal Code. A recurring challenge in the technical assessment of low-velocity projectile devices is determining whether a device is capable of causing serious bodily injury and therefore meeting the Criminal Code definition of a firearm. These assessments require scientifically defensible data regarding the performance and injury potential of projectiles fired from such devices. To support these assessments, SFSS is exploring a means of experimentally determine V50 ballistic limit velocities for a variety of projectiles commonly used in airguns, airsoft devices, and similar low-velocity projectile devices. The resulting information may support firearms classification activities and contribute to our broader technical understanding of projectile performance and injury potential. Canada is particularly interested in research that expands upon the methodology and findings presented in AD3, AD4, and AD5. Unlike the referenced studies, which focused on a limited number of airguns and projectile types, the potential requirement may involve testing a broader range of projectiles and devices commonly encountered in firearms-classification activities, including airguns, airsoft devices, and other low-velocity projectile devices.

title: F108--Groundwater Remediation

This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is a request for quotations (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 562910 with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees. The Product Service Code for this procurement is F108. The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Officer 01 is seeking to purchase the supplies or services described in the following Statement of Work. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation notice synopsizing a solicitation to satisfy the requirements of RFO FAR 5.2 and RFO FAR 5.3. All interested parties should register via SAM.gov interested vendors list. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: Fuel Storage Services at West Oahu, HI
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE: This notice is being published in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 5.101 requiring dissemination of information for proposed contract actions. This is a notice of intent to make a single source award contract and is not a request for competitive proposals. The statutory authority for the use of other than full and open competition procedure for this procurement is prescribed by FAR 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy the agency�s requirements. DLA Energy intends to issue a four-year base, with one, five-year option period and six one-month options firm fixed price single source award contract to IES Downstream, LLC (IES), in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1), Only One Responsible Source. The contract will provide services with the capability to receive via Tanker/Barge and Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH)/Red Hill (RH) tank farm and commercial/refinery pipeline, store, protect, and ship Aviation Turbine Fuel Grades Jet-A, JP-5 and Naval Distillate Fuel Grade F-76 via Tanker/Barge, JBPHH pipeline, and tank truck with a storage fill capacity of 2,051,000 barrels (BBLS). Background: IES provides contract services for the receipt and distribution of aviation fuel at West Oahu, Hawaii. Currently, the company receives Government-owned Aviation Turbine Fuel Grades Jet-A and JP-5) and Naval Distillate Fuel Grade F-76 via tanker/barge and contractor furnished pipeline system. This arrangement involves the unloading of fuel and its subsequent handling within IES's facilities. The Government intends to award a follow-on contract for these services at West Oahu, Hawaii, scheduled for Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27). This upcoming contract specifies an annual throughput requirement of 3,500,000 barrels of Aviation Turbine Fuel and Naval Distillate Fuel. To fulfill the requirement would require the construction of a pipeline and subsequent connection point to the Government�s pipeline by the start of the performance period (October 26, 2027). Competitive Environment: There are no planned actions to address barriers that would create a more competitive procurement environment for dock services at West Oahu, Hawaii. Objectives: The objective of the contract is to ensure uninterrupted support for the government customers' Jet and Naval Distillate fuel needs.

title: Stage 1 - Waskesiu Sanitary Upgrades, Prince Albert National Park
description: 5P468-26-0271/A Stage 1 - Waskesiu Sanitary Upgrades, Prince Albert National Park BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS TO BIDDERS (SI) This is a two stage selection process. Bidders responding to this selection process are requested to submit a bid in two stages. This posting is the first stage (Stage One) of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage will evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers; the second stage (Stage Two) will invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Upon award of contract in Stage Two the pre-qualification list will expire and will not be used in any other solicitation. The qualification list will expire within 180 days or upon award of a contract in Stage Two, whichever is earlier, and the prequalification list will not be used in any other solicitation. Following the evaluation of the submissions of Stage One, bidders will be advised of their qualification result and the status of the tender. Parks Canada reserves the right to re-issue Stage One via a /B solicitation if it is determined there is insufficient competition to proceed with Stage Two. Bidders that have qualified in Stage One /A will not be required to resubmit on the Stage One /B. Bidders that failed to demonstrate compliance on the Stage One /A may resubmit and will be considered in Stage One /B. Stage Two Bidders will be provided an INVITATION TO TENDER (ITT) for further qualifications and the financial evaluation in relation to the specifications and drawings. Please note that the ITT used in Stage 2 of this process will be a Two-Envelope ITT with an Indigenous Participation Plan (IPP) and a price evaluation component. LIST OF PRE-QUALIFIED BIDDERS: A list of pre-qualified bidders from Stage One will not be released. Contract award notice of the successful bidder of Stage Two will be posted on http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities PARTNER WITH ANOTHER BUSINESS: Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business” REQUIREMENT 5P468-26-0271/A Stage 1 - Waskesiu Sanitary Upgrades, Prince Albert National Park Parks Canada requires the services of a contractor for the rehabilitation of the sanitary sewer system within the Waskesiu Townsite and Beaver Glen Campground, in the Prince Albert National Park, SK. The Work is comprised of the following: 1 Preparation of existing pipe for liner system. 2 Installation of Cured In Place Pipe liner within the existing pipe. 3 Service connection reinstatement 4 CCTV Inspections of sanitary sewer lines To assist with bonding and insurance requirements, this project is estimated at a value between $500,001 > $ 1,000,000 Taxes extra. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work no later than March 31, 2028. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

description: L’objet de l'accord cadre porte sur la fourniture d’instruments météorologiques et prestations associées au profit des centres appartenant à la Direction de l’Ingénierie et de l’Expertise (DIE) de direction générale de l’armement. Il s'agit d'un accord­-cadre composite mono­-attributaire, composé de deux parties : Une part à bons de commande conformément aux dispositions de l’article R.2362-8 au Code de la Commande Publique (CCP) et une part à marchés subséquents conformément aux articles R.2362-1 à R.2362-7 du CCP. Pour la part à bons de commandes : la fourniture, l’installation, la mise en service et formation et d’instruments météorologiques et leur maintien en condition opérationnelle Les prestations qui pourront être réalisées dans le cadre de ce présent projet d’accord­-cadre sont notamment : Famille 1: Mesure de la température. Famille 2 : Mesure de la pression atmosphérique. Famille 3 : Mesure de l’humidité, Famille 4 : Mesure du vent en surface Famille 5 : Mesure des précipitations Famille 6 : Mesure du rayonnement Famille 7 : Mesure de la visibilité Famille 8 : Observation du temps présent et passé et de l’état du sol, Famille 9 : Observation et mesure des propriétés des nuages Famille 10 : Accessoires Les marchés subséquents préciseront certaines prestations ou fournitures ultérieures, dont les caractéristiques et les modalités d’exécution sont non définies dans l’accord-cadre. Les prestations seront réalisées au profit de : DGA Essais de missiles Site Gironde : Saint¬ Médard en­ Jalles (33), DGA Essais de missiles Site Landes : Biscarrosse (40),DGA Essais de missiles Site Méditerranée Toulon, Levant et Coudon (83), DGA Techniques navales Site de Toulon (83), DGA Techniques navales Site de Brest (29), DGA Essais de missiles Bâtiment d’Essais et de Mesures Monge, DGA Essais de missiles Station d’Essais et de Mesures de Quimper (29), DGA Essais de missiles Station d'Essais de Mesures d'Hourtin (SEMH) (33), DGA Essais propulseurs : Saclay (91), DGA Maîtrise de l'information : Bruz (35), DGA Essais en vol Site de Cazaux (33), DGA Essais en vol Site d’Istres (13), DGA Maîtrise NRBC : Vert Le Petit (91), DGA Techniques aérospatiales : Balma (31), DGA Techniques hydrodynamiques : Val de Reuil (27), DGA Techniques terrestres Site de Bourges (18), DGA Techniques terrestres Site d’Angers (49). La date limite de remise des candidatures est fixée au 12/11/2026 à 16:00 heures (Heure de Paris). La date et l'heure limites inscrites à la rubrique 5.1.12 sont au format UTC. Il s'agit d'un Marché de défense ou de sécurité. Le présent projet de marché fait l'objet d'une procédure formalisée négociée avec mise en concurrence et publicité préalable, conformément aux dispositions des articles L.2324-1, L.2324-3, R.2324-1, R.2324-3, et R.2361-8 à R.2361-12 du CCP. L'accord-­cadre est conclu pour une durée de validité de 7 (sept) ans. Le montant maximum s'élève à 7 000 000 € HT, indiqués à la rubrique 2.1.3 ci­-après. Ce montant maximum correspond à une estimation globale pour le projet d'accord­-cadre, sans engagement de la part de l'État de l'atteindre. Le montant maximum indiqué en rubriques 2 et 5 ci-après est en euros hors taxe. Les candidats doivent indiquer dans leur candidature s'ils se présentent en tant que candidat individuel ou groupement d'opérateurs économiques. Il est interdit aux candidats de présenter pour l'accord­-cadre plusieurs offres en agissant à la fois : 1. en qualité de candidats individuels et de membres d'un ou plusieurs groupements ; 2. en qualité de membres de plusieurs groupements. La forme du groupement n'est pas imposée. La composition des groupements peut être modifiée, et il est possible d'en constituer de nouveaux entre la remise des candidatures et la remise des offres initiales si tous les membres du nouveau groupement, présenté au stade des offres, ont été autorisés au stade des candidatures à présenter une offre ou à y participer, au moins en tant que sous-contractant accepté dans la phase candidature. Le groupement nouvellement constitué doit respecter les exigences relatives aux capacités des candidats. De plus, les dispositions des articles R.2142-23 et R.2342-14 du CCP s’appliquent. La fourniture de tous les éléments/documents listés en rubriques 2.1.6 et 5.1.9 est primordiale, sous peine de rejet de la candidature de l’opérateur économique. Le présent avis de marché ne concerne que la PHASE CANDIDATURE. Le dossier de consultation sera envoyé ultérieurement aux candidats admis à soumissionner. Il pourra être fait application des dispositions de l'article R.2394-1 du CCP (clauses de réexamen relative aux conditions de variation des prix, à des évolutions, aux références des instruments de météorologie, aux situations de crise et rajout de sites bénéficiaires).

title: Ireland – Works for complete or part construction and civil engineering work – R232 Glenmore Bridge Widening and Road Realignment Scheme
description: Donegal County Council proposes to upgrade the section of the existing R232 that crosses Lough Ultan River at Glenmore approx. 4.7km West of Pettigo. The proposed road will provide an improved alignment and cross section. The project will include: a) A new concrete extension to the existing masonry bridge crossing the Lough Ultan River on the realigned R232. b) The realignment of approximately 0.7km of road infrastructure and cross-sectional improvements. Works will include, but are not limited to, the following: - Earthworks including excavation and filling and the disposal of surplus material; - Overhead telecom service diversion; - Drainage works; - Pavement construction; - Works on and adjacent to live carriageways along a narrow and winding alignment; - Works adjacent to woodland; - Works on and adjacent to the existing watercourse, including temporary diversion (piping); - Works on and adjacent to the existing bridge structure, including partial removal of wingwalls, repair and repointing to the bridge stonework; - Traffic management including temporary traffic routing to keep the Regional Road open; - In-situ concrete construction of bridge extension components; - Fabrication and erection of precast arch bridge elements; - Safety barriers, timber post fencing; - Tie-ins to the existing road at either end; - Tie-ins with a number of farm accesses.

title: Incubator Programs for Secure Facilities and Networks at Universities
description: Pursuant to Section 1071 of Public Law 119-60, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (Section 1071), the Department of War (DoW) is conducting an assessment on the feasibility, advisability, and potential benefits of establishing incubator programs for the development, operation, and sustainment of secure facilities and networks at select institutions of higher education. This RFI seeks detailed information from institutions capable of: Establishing or expanding secure facilities and networks Accelerating the transition of innovative technologies to DoW mission use Increasing availability of secure spaces to support classified research and development (R&D), prototyping, secure collaboration, and research transition activities Expanding the cleared technical workforce Serving as a regional innovation hub supporting multi-tenant use (DoW, industry, and academia) Long-term economic sustainment with significant non-federal cost-sharing The Department intends to use RFI responses to inform its assessment to Congress on the feasibility, advisability, and potential benefits to the Department of establishing the incubator programs described in Section 1071. The purpose of this information request is to ensure that any potential assessment provided to Congress and any subsequently authorized incubator program are grounded in realistic construction, security, governance, and sustainment planning. Early identification of cost, compliance, and institutional commitment factors is intended to reduce risk for both the U.S. Government and participating institutions. This RFI is for planning and assessment purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation.

description: This is a Notice of Intent to Sole Source published in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) RFO 5.101(a) Pre-solicitation notice requirements and (FAR) RFO 12.102 Restricting Competition. This Notice of Intent is for a proposed award of an open market sole source award to EATON CORPORATION for a Service and Preventative Maintenance contract for the following UPS equipment. EATON UPS MODEL 9390-160 - EH456CBC09 9390-160 EE423CAB13 93PM EN493UXX02 93PM EN373UXX02 93PM ES265UXX06 93PM ES262UXX03 93PM ET074UXX02 93PM ES255UXX04 The location of service will be at the Hershel "Woody" Williams VA Medical Center 1540 Spring Valley Drive Huntington, WV 25704-9300. As the original equipment manufacturer (OEM), and an ISO9001 certified supplier, Eaton Corporation (formerly: Eaton Electrical Inc. and Powerware ) is the provider of factory-supported, factory trained, factory authorized and factory certified service for your critical UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) equipment. Eaton offers power quality services for its UPS products, as well as for related equipment such as power distribution units (PDUs), batteries, alternative energy devices and Cutler-Hammer switchgear. Eaton also services products from legacy brands, including Powerware, Exide Electronics, Best Power, IPM, Deltec and Lortec. Eaton is the only authorized provider of service support with the Eaton developed proprietary service software for 3-phase Eaton UPS products. Eaton does not train, certify or support independent third party service providers to deliver or service Eaton UPS and power quality products. Due to its lack of training on competitor s platforms Eaton does not service non-Eaton branded power quality equipment. Eaton only works on its own branded equipment or devices it s been certified to fully support and maintain (e.g., flywheels, static transfer switches). No other service supplier is authorized to possess Eaton proprietary (copyrighted) software, repair documentation, processes or materials. description: Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC) Procurement, on behalf of The Office of Financial Research (OFR) and the Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC), intends to contract with London Stock Exchange Group PLC, 10 Paternoster Square London EC4M 7LS United Kingdom. There is no competitive vendor or regulatory agency that provides these datasets. London Stock Exchange (LSEG) has exclusive rights to the required Masterfile data. On July 21, 2010, President Obama signed the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the "Dodd-Frank Act"), which created the Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC) and the Office of Financial Research (OFR). The FSOC is charged with three primary purposes: to identify risks to the financial stability of the United States, to promote market discipline, and to respond to emerging threats to the stability of the U.S. financial system. The FSOC brings together the expertise of federal financial regulators, state regulators, and an insurance expert appointed by the President. The mission of the OFR is to support the Financial Stability Oversight Council (�the Council�) in promoting financial stability by: collecting data on behalf of the Council; providing such data to the Council and member agencies; standardizing the types and formats of data reported and collected; performing applied research and essential long-term research; developing tools for risk measurement and monitoring; performing other related services; making the results of the activities of the OFR available to financial regulatory agencies; and assisting such member agencies in determining the types of formats of data authorized by Dodd-Frank Act to be collected by such member agencies. Pursuant to its mandate, OFR has a Memorandum of Understanding with the Depository Trust and Clearing Corporation (DTCC) for DTCC National Securities Clearing Corporation (NSCC's) ETF PCF Portfolio Data, Historical Data, and Near-Time Supplemental File. This data is provided to OFR from DTCC, however the agreement requires OFR to maintain its own license with the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) for LSEG�s Stock Exchange Daily Official List (SEDOL) Masterfile�. The SEDOL Masterfile is a unique securities identifier specific to the London Stock Exchange. The OFR and FSOC currently use the proposed contractor�s sole source product for the qFSI monitor and annual report content pursuant to its mission to deliver an annual assessment of the state of the U.S. financial system, as required by the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE. A request for more information or a copy of the solicitation will not be considered an affirmative response to this Special Notice. Telephone responses or inquiries to this Special Notice will not be accepted. The period of performance for the purchase order is anticipated to be a twelve (12) month base period. All responses must include sufficient evidence that clearly shows your company is capable of providing the content described in this notice. Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no written response is received by the aforementioned deadline that clearly demonstrates an ability to meet all requirements, and that is more advantageous to the Government, TCSC will make award on a sole source basis to London Stock Exchange Group PLC.
